title: Anticanonical nonvanishing from smooth semipositivity
main_claim: Thm 1.1: if X is smooth connected projective and -K_X has a smooth semipositive Hermitian metric, then H^0(X,-mK_X) is nonzero for some m>0. The route: Thm 2.1 (the DPS/CDP structure theorem keeping a compact-torus monodromy) reduces to a torus-invariant section on the rationally connected factor Z, then descends via the finite étale norm. The invariant section comes from Thm 7.2, which uses a Rosenlicht quotient, the smooth invariant transfer (Prop 7.1) and Thm 1.2. Thm 1.2 says: on a no-forms Z, if -K_Z+D carries a finite-adjoint-volume psh metric and L carries a bounded psh metric, then aL+bD is effective. It is proved by induction on dimension, using a cotangent slope bound (Thm 4.2), a maximal linear system giving a smaller base with adjoint rank one (Lemmas 6.1–6.2), and two-metric transfer (Prop 5.1).

issues.description: Notation clash: P is defined as det Q but written as (wedge^rank Q*)**, which is det Q*. The proof uses P = det Q* (generically f*K_S plus (e-1)E at multiple fibres), consistent with D - P = D + det Q. The mathematics is unaffected.
issues.evidence: 'Q = T_Z/F, P = det Q = (wedge^{rank Q} Q*)**' versus 'D - P = D + det Q' and the vanishing order e-1 of f*K_S -> P.

issues.description: The paper applies the HN/tensor-slope theory of Greb–Kebekus–Peternell and the algebraicity criterion of Campana–Păun (Thm 1.1) to real movable classes alpha that may lie on the boundary of the movable cone. The paper asserts these citations cover such classes; I did not check this beyond the citation.
issues.evidence: alpha comes from the BDPP supporting hyperplane in Cor 4.3 and need not be rational.

coverage:
Read the whole PDF (27 pp; the LaTeX section files are missing from build/source, so I used pdftotext). Checked step by step:
- Thm 2.1 deck-group reduction: finite isometry group of the Ricci-flat factor; centralizer and commutator trick for a lattice; algebraic torus via a projective representation and Zariski closure.
- Lemma 2.2 (finite étale norm).
- Lemma 3.1 (prepared model).
- Lemma 4.1: Bergman L^2 bound gives psi <= (e-1)log|z1|^2 + C, and the frame comparison on D-P has the right sign.
- Thm 4.2: contradiction from the sum over nonpositive HN slopes; tensor slope bound.
- Cor 4.3.
- Lemma 6.1: chi(K+mL) has constant term (-1)^d; DPS hard Lefschetz; stabilization of the saturated subsheaf; M.alpha <= 0.
- Lemma 6.2: degrees in interpolation identity (6.4) and order identity (6.5) checked by hand; rank one via clearing vertical poles with big H0 and pi_*O(K_{Y/Z}) = O_Z; point-base case.
- Prop 5.1: c_T normalization; Bergman-weight identification with -log V_j; bounds (5.5), (5.6), (5.9), (5.10); lower and upper bounds on Psi; D_S supported on bad primes; lifting.
- Prop 7.1: Berndtsson positivity on the orthogonal invariant summand.
- Thm 7.2: invariant wedge of fundamental vector fields; T-fixed = G-fixed; C(Y)^G = C(S).
- Final descent to X.
No sign, constant or quantifier error found.
sibling_notes: Family 068 siblings (Bounded metrics, Metric descent, Cohomological transfer, Invariant indices, Exact orders, Integrable metrics) all reported no_gap_found with the same transfer/Bergman machinery. Unlike those, this paper is self-contained: it proves its own versions of the torus-monodromy cover theorem (Thm 2.1) and the invariant transfer (Prop 7.1) rather than citing companion papers, and it does not rely on LMPTX Thm 4.1 (replaced by its own Lemma 4.1 / Thm 4.2).
